function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick guide on where you can order a cake—plus a few handy tips to make sure you get exactly what you’re craving.

---

## 1️⃣ Local Bakeries (Best for Freshness & Customization)

| City / Region | Popular Options | How to Order |
|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
| **New York** | *Magnolia Bakery*, *Baked by Melissa*, *The Cake Shop* | Call or visit their website; many accept online orders via their own portal or through platforms like **DoorDash** or **Uber Eats**. |
| **Los Angeles** | *Bakeri*, *Martha & Sons*, *The Sweet Spot* | Most have a dedicated online ordering page; otherwise, use **Postmates** or **Instacart**. |
| **Chicago** | *Krispy Kreme*, *The Sweet Life*, *Sweet Treats* | Order directly on their site or call. |
| **London** | *The Cake Kitchen*, *Cakes & Bites*, *Bake & Deliver* | Book online or call; many also partner with **Deliveroo**. |
| **Toronto** | *Cake & Co.*, *Sweet & Sassy*, *The Sweet Spot* | Use their website or order via **SkipTheDishes**. |

> **Tip:** If you’re looking for a custom design (e.g., birthday, wedding, corporate), most local shops offer a “custom cake” service. Just let them know your theme, size, and flavor preferences.

---

## 2️⃣ National Online Delivery Services

| Service | What They Offer | How to Order |
|---------|-----------------|--------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated selection of iconic regional cakes (think New York cheesecake, Chicago deep-dish cake). | Browse the catalog, pick a cake, and place an order. Delivery is nationwide. |
| **Cake Delivery** | Same‑day delivery in major cities, plus a wide range of flavors. | Choose your city, pick a cake, and schedule delivery. |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Some grocery stores deliver pre‑made cakes (often from local bakeries). | Search “cake” in Amazon Fresh, add to cart, and choose delivery slot. |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, artisanal cakes from independent bakers worldwide. | Find a seller, customize your order, and arrange shipping. |

> **Pro Tip:** Check the delivery window and confirm the cake will arrive fresh. Many sites allow you to specify a delivery time or even a “delivery date” for special occasions.

---

## 3️⃣ Food‑Delivery Apps (Convenient for Quick Orders)

| App | Where It Works | How to Order |
|-----|----------------|--------------|
| **DoorDash** | Major U.S. cities, some Canadian cities | Search “cake” or “bakery,” select a shop, and place an order. |
| **Uber Eats** | Global coverage | Look for “cakes” or “desserts” in the app. |
| **Postmates** | U.S. cities | Search “cake” or “bakeries.” |
| **Deliveroo** | UK, Ireland, Australia | Search “cake” or “bakery.” |
| **SkipTheDishes** | Canada | Search “cake” or “bakery.” |

> **Heads‑Up:** These apps often charge a delivery fee, so factor that into your budget. Some also offer “scheduled delivery” for birthdays or events.

---

## 4️⃣ Specialty & Gourmet Options

| Specialty | Why It Stands Out | Ordering |
|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| **Artisan Chocolate Cakes** | Hand‑crafted chocolate layers, premium ingredients | Order from boutique chocolatiers like **Ladurée** or **Godiva**. |
| **Gluten‑Free & Vegan Cakes** | Allergy‑friendly, plant‑based | Sites like **Vegan Cake Delivery** or local vegan bakeries. |
| **Custom Wedding Cakes** | Large, multi‑tiered designs | Contact a wedding cake specialist; many offer virtual consultations. |

---

## 5️⃣ How to Make Your Order Smooth

1. **Decide on Size & Flavor** – Standard sizes: 8”, 10”, 12”, 16”.  
2. **Check Availability** – Some cakes sell out fast (especially for holidays).  
3. **Read Reviews** – Look at recent customer photos and comments.  
4. **Confirm Delivery Time** – Specify a “delivery window” if possible.  
5. **Ask About Cancellation Policy** – In case plans change.  

---

### Want More Specific Recommendations?

If you tell me your city or ZIP code, I can pull up the top-rated bakeries and delivery options in your area. Feel free to share any dietary restrictions or special occasion details (birthday, wedding, corporate event) so I can tailor the suggestions even further.

Happy cake hunting! 🍰
